_comment: Explicit-clip footage catalogue for Prisoners (2013). id = 'clip:<HH:MM:SS.s>'. depicts/chars describe what the timestamp ACTUALLY shows on screen (verified from frame montages), not what narration claims. One clip = one primary moment; 1-2 depicts tags max (see docs/TAGGING_GUIDE.md). Catalogued content-first from the 34-beat descriptions (beat list timestamps were from a different cut and are unreliable; located each beat via transcript + frames).

shots.action: Keller and Ralph in orange hunting gear aim a rifle at a deer in the snowy winter forest
the Dover family walks up the street to the Birch home for Thanksgiving, Anna on Keller's shoulders, Grace carrying a dish
the adults prepare the Thanksgiving meal in the Birch kitchen, cutting venison
the two families relax together in the Birch living room, Franklin playing his trumpet
Anna and Joy stand before the adults asking permission to walk to the Dover house; last time the girls are seen together (Ralph not visible in this shot)
Keller searches the basement workshop looking for the missing girls
the four parents in the Birch living room realize the girls are gone, panic setting in
Detective Loki eats alone at the diner, introducing the character
night raid in the rain - police converge on the RV (faces not identifiable in the dark/rain; Loki and Alex not facially verifiable in this shot)
forensics personnel process the impounded RV under bright garage lights (wide shot, individual faces not identifiable; Loki present in scene but not facially verifiable here)
Nancy sits numb and grieving at the table, Franklin in the background of the Birch home
Grace lies in bed, drugged and grieving over the missing girls
Loki explains to Keller there is no evidence and Alex has the mind of a child, so he must be released
Keller, anguished, reacts to Loki telling him there is no proof to hold the suspect
Captain Richards at his desk presses Loki over the release decision while Loki stands across from him
Loki stands his ground defending the decision to release the suspect, then turns to leave the captain's office
at the station Loki, arms crossed, tells Keller they have no evidence to hold Alex and warns him to go home (Keller's back to camera in foreground)
close on an agitated Keller insisting Alex confessed ('are you sure that's what he said'), realizing the police will not act on his accusation
Bob Taylor, a strange young man with glasses and curly hair, sits on the couch being questioned; his behavior is off (introduction of Bob)
Loki questions Bob Taylor during a door-to-door interview
Keller waits in his truck at night watching the lit cabin, before abducting Alex (real abduction scene; the beat's listed 28:30-32:30 range is actually the unrelated priest/corpse investigation)
a hooded figure is led away in the dark during the abduction (silhouette; Keller/Alex not facially verifiable in this shot)
Holly Jones, Alex's aunt, sits calmly in her armchair answering Loki's questions; no red flags raised
Keller beats a bound, bloodied Alex on the bathroom floor of the abandoned apartment
closer angle in the tiled bathroom: Keller grips and strikes the bloodied Alex, whose battered face is visible
Franklin stands conflicted and shaken over the hunched, bloodied Alex in the bathroom
close on Keller shouting, anguished and unravelling, as he interrogates the prisoner during the beating
Keller forces the bloodied Alex against the sink as the torture intensifies, Franklin present in the bathroom
Nancy at the vigil at night, holding a candle, grieving among the crowd
dedicated close-up of Nancy and Grace grieving together among the candles at the night vigil
rows of candles and a teddy bear at the night candlelight vigil for the missing girls (wide community shot, no single character in focus)
Loki moves through the vigil crowd scanning faces, watching for a suspect
a hooded figure flees over a fence into the dark woods as Loki gives chase (figure not facially identifiable)
a hooded figure runs through the dark woods, silhouetted against the distant vigil lights (face not identifiable)
Franklin and Nancy at home, shaken and conflicted over their part in holding and hurting Alex
Keller returns to the locked torture box in the abandoned building to continue interrogating Alex, a photo of the missing girls on the wall
Grace approaches and confronts a distraught Keller in the hallway, sensing something is wrong; the family is unraveling
Keller, hooded, stands outside Bob Taylor's place in a desolate lot before breaking in
Keller searches inside Bob Taylor's place and finds the disturbing evidence (boxes of children's clothes and maze drawings)
Loki confronts a nervous, smiling Bob Taylor at his door before taking him in
Loki slides a photo of the bloodstained clothes across the table to show Keller the blood evidence from Bob
Keller, eyes closed and anguished, reacts to the blood evidence Loki has shown him
Bob Taylor hunches in the interrogation room obsessively drawing mazes, watched through the one-way glass
Bob breaks free and grabs a gun in the interrogation room as Loki and officers struggle to stop him
Bob backed against the interrogation-room wall, the gun in his hand, as Loki and an officer try to bring him down
Bob raises the gun under his own chin as the officers shout for him to stop
Bob slumps bloodied on the floor after shooting himself, Loki standing over him

daytime dig at Bob Taylor's property: forensics in white suits excavate while detectives watch; the lab reveals the clothes had tags on, the blood was pig's blood and the kids' bodies are mannequins, meaning Bob was a copycat and the girls are still missing (wide shot, faces not facially verifiable)
Grace, on the phone in the bedroom, gets the call that one of the girls has been found alive ('Yeah, this is she... Wait, is she?')
Nancy and Grace lean over the recovered Joy in her hospital bed, desperate for her to respond and tell them about Anna
Keller returns to Holly's house, claiming he wants to fix her door as penance; Holly, behind the storm-door glass, invites him in (the trap)
Holly in her kitchen seen past Keller, making tea and talking, the tension building before anything is revealed
Holly raises a revolver and points it at Keller across the kitchen, turning the scene (Keller's back in foreground)
Holly draws a revolver on Keller in her kitchen, revealing she is the kidnapper; she and her late husband abducted the children as their 'war with God'
close on Keller at gunpoint in the kitchen, forced to comply and drink the drugged tea, his helplessness setting in
Holly, gun trained on Keller by the car, calmly confesses they took Alex first and that she kept the girls; tells Keller his daughters are 'under there'
at gunpoint Holly forces a bound Keller down into the hidden pit in her yard at night (very dark; both faces dimly visible)
in a hospital corridor Loki is told to go notify Holly Jones, the lead that sends him to her house
Loki arrives at the green front door of Holly's house, numbered 1634, and steps inside
Loki bursts into Holly's house, gun drawn, shouting for her to show her hands moments before the shootout in which he kills Holly and saves Anna
Loki, gun drawn and aimed, shouts for Holly to show her hands inside her house
a dark, low-angle struggle on the kitchen floor during the shooting (faces not identifiable in the dark)
Holly raises a gun toward Loki in the dim hallway
Loki, shot in the struggle, doubles over and staggers, wounded
a car races down a dark, wet country road at night as Loki rushes the rescued Anna to the hospital (no faces visible)
hospital corridor aftermath: a recovering Anna in a wheelchair tended by Grace, with Nancy and Joy nearby, the families reunited

night excavation of Holly's property after the case; a lone figure lingers at the dig site (silhouette), the moment before the faint whistle from Keller's hidden pit closes the film (faces not verifiable)
